spec_features.spec_quote: We do cap by `max_steps` and a hard token budget.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:95 `for step in range(1, loop_cfg.max_steps + 1)` bounds the loop (default max_steps=12, config.py:91). loop.py:96-98 `if usage.total >= model_cfg.total_token_budget: stop_reason='token_budget'; break` actually compares the accumulated usage (usage.add at loop.py:105) and breaks. total_token_budget=120_000 at config.py:55.
spec_features.notes: Both halves enforced and change execution. The wall_seconds value (loop.py:139,164) is measured but never compared to any deadline.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard per-run total token budget ... Bounds worst-case cost and runaway megaturns

spec_features.evidence: tool_specs only appends the give_up ToolSpec when escape_hatch is true (tools.py:47-56). dispatch handles it (tools.py:167-170) setting self.gave_up=True. is_terminal() returns self.gave_up (tools.py:192), and loop.py:135-137 breaks with stop_reason='gave_up'. So when on, it is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and honored, but gated on escape_hatch which defaults to 'off' (config.py:78; headline default has hatch=off), so in the default/headline arm the exit is not available to the subject. Hence narrower than an always-available exit.

spec_features.feature_name: subject told it may give up / declare blocked
spec_features.spec_quote: whether the agent is told it *may* declare the task blocked/give up
spec_features.evidence: When escape_hatch=='on', build_system appends _HATCH_NOTE (loop.py:46-47): 'If you become convinced the task cannot be completed, you may call give_up with a clear reason instead of continuing.' This instruction text is delivered to the subject and its referenced tool is actually built and honored. The continue_nudge (config.py:94-97) also mentions give_up, but that tool is only present when hatch is on.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction delivered only in the hatch=on arm; absent in the default headline arm. The continue_nudge references give_up even when the tool is not advertised (potentially dangling in hatch=off runs).

spec_features.spec_quote: we keep a `neutral` arm to avoid the criticism that we *prompted* the model into despair
spec_features.evidence: _PRESSURE['neutral']='' (loop.py:31) so build_system adds no pressure text for neutral, vs 'high' which adds 'Do not give up — keep going...' (loop.py:33-37). FactorCell defaults to pressure='neutral' (config.py:76) and RunConfig.headline()/default uses a single FactorCell() (config.py:135-145). So the neutral framing genuinely changes the system prompt and is the executed default.
spec_features.notes: It is a real, enforced factor that alters prompt content; not just prose. The motivation in code is experimental defensibility, not subject welfare.
